This Gorgeous Tiny House from Tasmania Hides the Most Unique Vintage Finds
34 photos
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes
To simply say that the Little Keepsake is beautiful would be an understatement. A treasure trove of real vintage finds, personal items from the owner’s previous residences, and impeccable contemporary styling, this Tasmanian tiny house goes far beyond the concept of custom design. This is tiny house styling and craftsmanship at its finest, with the kind of inherent warmth and individuality that outshine all conventional luxury.
There’s really nothing out there quite like the Little Keepsake – more than a spectacular house on wheels, built and styled with stunning attention to detail, this unique abode is like a living museum and art gallery designed to give certain precious objects a second life. Just as its lovely name suggests, this custom tiny house is filled with objects that the owner had enjoyed previously and didn’t want to let go, as well as authentic vintage finds.
Many tiny homes try to replicate a vintage aesthetic through style choices, but the Little Keepsake incorporates actual vintage items and repurposed objects into what can be described as an impeccable contemporary style. In other words, this house is by no means a messy collection of “old” things, scattered around a cramped interior – it’s a luxurious home equipped with modern conveniences, ready for comfortable living, and furnished impeccably.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes “A tiny home that celebrates imperfection, history, and individuality” – this is how its builder, the family-owned Artisan Tiny Homes, based, in Wivenhoe, Tasmania, describes it. It all started with a customer who wanted to find a new home not just for themselves, but for their personal collection as well. That is how, although brand-new, this tiny house ended up hiding more exciting vintage finds than a museum on wheels, masterfully integrated throughout.
Even from the outside, the contemporary-style corrugated metal exterior with timber insertions gently incorporates vintage windows. A striking bright green door hints at the home’s artistic and quirky interior, while elegant French back doors provide a second entrance. Inside, guests will discover a unique mix of old, repurposed doors (several of them), stained glass accents (a beautiful artistic touch), and old timber items everywhere.
Perhaps one of the most spectacular things about Little Keepsake is that it doesn’t just pack a selection of vintage and repurposed objects in the lounge, for instance. Just like a treasure trove, every single area is worth exploring, in order to discover the “secret” vintage finds. It even has one of the most beautiful bathrooms, by far, you’ll ever see in a tiny house, and there are statement pieces in almost every part of the house.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes On the ground floor, an open living room is flanked by the kitchen and the bathroom, while both lofts serve as spacious bedrooms. Benefitting from a nine-meter (29.5 feet) length and a height of slightly over four meters (13 feet), this gooseneck-type home on wheels boasts ample floor space for a full-size kitchen, a spectacular bathroom, and two comfortable bedrooms in the loft area. Each loft includes staircase access, making this home a lot more comfortable for full-time living.
Little Keepsake has the dimensions, the functionality, and the thoughtful layout of an ideal family home. One of its main attractions is the huge U-shaped kitchen, which incorporates a classic Australian breakfast bar – large and strategically placed under a big window, as well as gorgeous cabinetry throughout.
The pastel green shade of the cabinets was chosen for its “gentle country feel”, and it complements the natural tone and texture of the timber countertops beautifully. The massive, copper sink is an absolute statement piece, coupled with vintage-style tapware and brightly-patterned fabrics for contrast.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes Full-size, premium appliances bring this kitchen into modern times, as well as the black-framed windows all-around that ingeniously mimic a panoramic effect. Filled with natural light, perfectly spacious for a family, and furnished with that custom cabinetry that provides ample storage space, this farmhouse-inspired kitchen feels almost cinematic.
The lounge itself is no more than a spacious transition area, big enough to fit a full-size sofa with a generous view thanks to the French doors, but the staircases are enough to elevate this entire space on their own. Especially the one close to the kitchen area, which leads to the main bedroom, is a true work of art. It displays timber spindles in various finishes and colors, which are actually vintage items in their original form.
Built-in storage is also elegantly incorporated into this staircase, and the interior design is further enriched with old stained glass accents high above the entrance door, plus a superb bespoke chandelier in a shade that of vibrant green that matches the kitchen cabinetry. Every single detail is impeccably integrated for a seamless look, where old meets new in a sophisticated way.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes The other staircase is conventionally-built, but it also hides a little vintage perk: another repurposed metal rod that becomes a practical handrail, in sharp contrast to the white, farmhouse-inspired staircase. Another statement piece that adds character to the lounge is the beautiful bathroom door – not inspired by, but an actual, old barn door that was reclaimed and given a second life.
Behind this heavy timber door, you’ll find one of the most unique, sophisticated tiny house bathrooms. A stunning copper sink takes center stage, paired perfectly with an old timber vanity, and vintage-style tapware. In sharp contrast, the shower cabin is luxuriously contemporary, a well-blended mix of green tiles and glass panels. All the storage space, including a dedicated laundry nook, is custom-built.
Upstairs, in the main loft, guests will also be delighted to discover custom-built wardrobes that look absolutely beautiful: emerald green adorned with vintage-style doorknobs and matching patterned wallpaper. The floor space of this walk-through loft bedroom has been wisely used to fit in those large custom cabinets, in addition to the queen-sized bed. A vintage swing door adds the right vintage accents, and large windows bring in natural light.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes The second loft is smaller, it only has a vintage nightstand as storage furniture, but what makes it extra comfortable are the numerous large windows, coupled with another big, vertical window at the top of the staircase.
Flooring throughout is waterproof laminate, and the house is equipped to be connected to all regular utilities. Perfect for accommodating up to four people, Little Keepsake is an excellent choice for families (a similar platform can be used for other builds, but this Tasmanian tiny house builder only does custom tiny homes.)
Little Keepsake’s uniqueness is the result of a visionary customer and a talented builder joining forces. Kerrie, the soul and force behind Artisan Tiny Homes, is an interior designer and an artist, which explains the stunning beauty of all the abodes rolled out from this workshop. Working with her husband Kevin, who is a builder and a restorer, and with their daughter who is a carpenter, Kerrie brings to life true works of art on wheels, unlike anything else on the market.
Photo: Artisan Tiny Homes Artisan Tiny Homes was established almost a decade ago, in 2018, and since then it has delivered just a little over 30 tiny homes, because it’s not about quantity and mass market, but about bringing art, soul, and craftsmanship into bespoke homes. I almost can’t imagine any of the owners of an Artisan tiny home selling their homes, precisely because they’re so unique and filled with passion in every detail – and that’s how it should be.
